en: Itivuttaka 105 Catukkanipāta Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus it was said. This is the meaning of what was said: “Brahmins, there are these four kinds of gifts. What four? The gift of material things, the gift of Dhamma, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of the Dhamma. These, brahmins, are the four kinds of gifts. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this: “The gift of material things is indeed excellent, And so too is the gift of fearlessness; But the gift of the Dhamma is supreme among them all, For it leads to the state beyond death. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. The Discourse on the Arising of Craving.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these four origins of craving where, for a bhikkhu, craving arises as it is arising."
Which four?
Monks, craving arises in a monk because of robes;
or, monks, craving arises in a monk because of almsfood.
“Monks, craving arises in a monk because of lodgings;
or, monks, craving arises in a monk because of ‘being this’ or ‘being that.
These, monks, are the four origins of craving where craving arises in a monk.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
"A person has craving as his companion..."
Wandering through a long course of existence,
one does not transcend the cycle of wandering from this state to another state.
Having understood this danger—
that craving is the origin of suffering—
one who is free from craving and without grasping...
“A mindful bhikkhu should wander.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The sixth [discourse].
